decisions.quote: Results replicated and extended past findings suggesting that acting extraverted produces hedonic benefits regardless of disposition. Positive affect increased and negative affect did not, even for participants acting out of character.
decisions.reason: Across both experiments, the authors explicitly conclude that they replicated Fleeson et al.'s (2002) core finding that acting extraverted increases positive affect regardless of trait disposition; the 'mixed' result mentioned in Study 1's discussion refers only to the novel ego-depletion extension on Stroop performance.

decisions.quote: We predicted that Fleeson et al.’s (2002) core findings would replicate. That is, our participants would be able to act as we instructed them, and acting extraverted would cause positive affect, regardless of disposition. Analyses also tested the idea that acting counterdispositionally can lead to increased negative affect. However, given hints from past research, we did not anticipate large negative affective consequences for acting out of character.
decisions.reason: McNiel and Fleeson (2006) is cited only in the introduction as background literature providing prior context on negative affect and state extraversion; the experiments are explicitly framed as a replication and extension of Fleeson et al. (2002) and never evaluate or compare results against McNiel and Fleeson (2006) as a replication target.

decisions.reason: McNiel, Lowman, and Fleeson (2010) is cited as background literature on state extraversion and affect to motivate the study's negative-affect extension rather than as an original finding re-tested by the present experiments, which explicitly target Fleeson et al. (2002).

parent_objection: The first review excludes McNiel&Fleeson2006 and McNiel/Lowman/Fleeson2010 as background. Source inspection shows a specific published finding:two studies assessed negative affect and failed to find the state-by-trait interaction suggesting a mood cost;the paper criticizes their small sample/within-subject designs and says the full mood consequences require clarification. Its own two studies deliberately test the same counterdispositional negative-affect interaction with new participants and a changed design,reporting no negative-affect cost. The codebook decides actual retesting,not whether authors call it an extension relative to Fleeson2002. Determine if each prior negative-affect study is genuinely re-tested or only motivates a different empirical claim. Changed design and an extension label alone cannot exclude a conceptual replication. Account for closest-chain rule from actual citation/design relationship rather than assuming every cited paper is a target. If insufficient,retain uncertainty. Fleeson2002successful outcome remains accepted. This is the second and final call,including mechanical retries.

blind_target.title: An intraindividual process approach to the relationship between extraversion and positive affect: Is acting extraverted as “good” as being extraverted?
blind_target.evidence_quote: We predicted that Fleeson et al.’s (2002) core findings would replicate. That is, our participants would be able to act as we instructed them, and acting extraverted would cause positive affect, regardless of disposition.
blind_target.outcome_quote: In sum, this study replicates the finding that, regardless of underlying trait disposition, extraverted behavior produces greater positive affect than introverted behavior.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The reported positive-affect benefit and/or absence of dispositional negative-affect cost agrees with this original’s findings. Cognitive depletion is a novel extension, not a failed replication of these mood findings.
